evidence.title: Postmortem: Helios load-test failure
evidence.text: # Postmortem: Helios load-test failure Hey team, just dropping the initial notes from our debugging session regarding the [[Helios]] environment issues we ran into yesterday. The Helios load-test failure was traced to a connection-pool exhaustion bug in the new Stripe usage-metering service under concurrent writes. When we ramped up the simulation to mimic peak traffic for Pulse, the metering service kept opening new connections without releasing them back to the pool properly during heavy transaction bursts. This directly starved the main database threads and cascaded into timeout errors across the rest of the stack. It's a pretty classic oversight, but definitely something we need to patch before we touch the [[Billing migration]] plans we discussed last week. I've opened a ticket to cap the pool size and implement aggressive backpressure on the client side. We'll rerun the suite once the fix lands in staging. Let's make sure we keep an eye on this in our next sync.

evidence.title: Aurora migration — risk assessment
evidence.text: # Aurora migration — risk assessment Hey everyone, dropping some notes here following our sync on the database infrastructure. As we push toward the [[Helios]] release next month, we need to make sure our underlying data layers can handle the spike in throughput without dropping events or spiking error rates on Pulse. Looking closely at the timeline and our current test runs, the main identified risk for the Aurora migration is replication lag under the increased session-write volume expected after the Helios launch. Since Pulse relies heavily on real-time session replay ingestion alongside continuous error tracking and performance analytics, even a brief delay in replica sync could cause temporary inconsistencies in the dashboard or back up our ingestion queues. We saw some minor latency spikes during the last load test when writes doubled, which points right to this bottleneck. Action items for this week: - Run another stress test simulating 3x normal write load against an [[Aurora migration]] staging cluster. - Check parameter tuning on the writer and reader instances to see if we can optimize the replication stream. - Coordinate with the frontend squad so we handle any potential read-after-write quirks gracefully in the UI if lag does creep in during peak hours. Let's keep discussions rolling in the main channel. I'll update this note once we have the new benchmark numbers back from staging.

evidence.title: Infra review — 2026-01-20
evidence.text: # Infra review — 2026-01-20 Good turnout today for the sync. Mostly went over the usual [[Pulse]] backend metrics, but we spent a good chunk of time diving into the current database setup and why everyone keeps getting paged at 3 AM. The main pain point continues to be manual maintenance on the self-hosted instances. Between disk space alerts, routine patching, and replication lag [[Helios]], the team is spending way too much time babysitting infrastructure instead of shipping features for [[Pulse]]. After looking at a few options, the team decided at the 2026-01-20 infra review to migrate the primary Postgres database from self-hosted to a managed provider (Aurora), to reduce on-call burden. Moving to Aurora should take a massive weight off the [[Aurora migration]] project backlog. We'll get automated backups, easier scaling, and—most importantly—fewer middle-of-the-night alerts for the engineering rotation. Will spin up a staging cluster next week to benchmark the read/write performance against our current setup. If the numbers look good, we'll draft a proper cutover timeline and share it with the rest of the crew.

evidence.title: API v2 deprecation — communications plan
evidence.text: # API v2 deprecation — communications plan Just wanted to drop a quick update here before our standup regarding the [[Pulse]] [[API v2 deprecation]] timeline and how we are looping in our user base. After sync'ing with the product team yesterday, we agreed that the messaging needs to be clear, direct, and give folks plenty of runway to move over to the current endpoints, especially the teams still leaning heavily on [[Aurora migration]] guides. Noah Fischer owns communicating the Pulse API v2 deprecation timeline to customers. He’s going to draft the initial announcement email and coordinate with support so they have templates ready for any incoming questions. We should make sure the documentation site is fully updated before that goes out, otherwise [[Helios]] and the rest of the support queue are going to get flooded with duplicate tickets. Let's touch base on Friday to review the draft.

evidence.title: Product roadmap — H1 2026
evidence.text: # Product roadmap — H1 2026 Here is our working outline for the upcoming half. The general focus for H1 2026 is on stabilizing our core data ingestion pipelines and improving overall dashboard responsiveness for larger teams. We want to make sure the core experience feels snappy before rolling out any major visual overhauls. A lot of this ties back to the ongoing work in [[Aurora migration]], which should give us the database performance headroom we need to support heavier query loads. On the feature side, we are currently tracking a few key initiatives. First, we need to finalize the scope for [[Helios]] so the design team can start exploring mockups by late Q1. Second, engineering has [[API v3]] on the docket as a background effort, primarily focused on cleaning up deprecated endpoints and improving developer documentation rather than rewriting the whole contract overnight. Customer feedback from the last few user interviews highlighted that session filtering still feels a bit clunky when dealing with high-volume noise. We should schedule a quick sync with support next week to pull some recent examples of those failing queries so the frontend squad has realistic test cases. As usual, this is a living document and will likely shift a bit once we lock in engineering capacity during our next planning retro. Feel free to drop comments or questions directly in the thread.

evidence.title: Re: Helios launch date — need options
evidence.text: # Re: Helios launch date — need options Hi Ravi and Amara, Thanks for walking through the latest telemetry and stress test numbers this morning. Looking at where we are with Pulse's underlying infrastructure and the remaining error tracking tweaks, I'm ready to make the call. I officially approve the revised Helios launch date of 2026-04-21, as of today, 2026-02-20. Please go ahead and coordinate with the board and our customer-facing teams to get everyone aligned on this timeline. Let's make sure our messaging is clear and that support has all the resources they need ahead of April. If anyone needs the approval in writing for the board pack, cite this email. Best, Priya Raman VP Product, Lumen Labs

evidence.title: Helios is live (one day late — TLS cert issue)
evidence.text: # Helios is live (one day late — TLS cert issue) Hey team, Just wanted to send a quick note that Helios actually shipped on 2026-04-22, which is one day after the approved 2026-04-21 date. Before anyone worries, I want to clarify right away that this had nothing to do with a repeat of the billing migration problem. The minor delay was entirely caused by a last-minute TLS certificate renewal issue in the staging environment that we needed to clear before pushing live. Everything looks stable in production now, and the metrics are flowing nicely into Pulse. Great job pushing through the final hurdle, everyone. Let's touch base at our usual time tomorrow to review the initial telemetry. Best, Amara

evidence.title: Helios launch date — need options
evidence.text: # Helios launch date — need options Hi Ravi and Amara, I just saw the notes from the latest staging run. Since the load test unfortunately failed at 4x volume, we clearly need to adjust our timeline before I put together the final slide deck for the board meeting. Could you both put together a couple of realistic revised launch options for Helios? I need to give the board a concrete target date by tomorrow afternoon so we can align expectations across the team. Let's grab a quick sync after stand-up to map out what remediation looks like and how many weeks we actually need to stabilize everything. Thanks, Priya

evidence.title: Re: Helios launch date — need options
evidence.text: # Re: Helios launch date — need options Hey Priya, Following up on our earlier thread—copying Ravi here as well. I think we need to push our timeline out a bit. Given the billing migration load-test failure we ran into yesterday, the engineering team is going to need some extra breathing room to sort out those bottlenecks before we make any further moves. How does 2026-04-21 sound to everyone as a revised date? That should give us enough runway to re-run the tests cleanly and verify everything is stable under peak traffic without rushing the final review. Let me know if that works for your schedules or if you want to hop on a quick call this afternoon to chat through it. Best, Amara

evidence.title: Re: Helios is live (one day late — TLS cert issue)
evidence.text: # Re: Helios is live (one day late — TLS cert issue) Hey everyone, Just wanted to send a quick note to say massive congratulations on getting Helios shipped! I know the last few weeks involved a ton of late nights, tight debugging sessions, and endless coffee, but the final result looks incredible. Priya, could you please take the lead on preparing the customer-facing messaging and release notes? Let's make sure our users clearly understand what's new and how they can start taking advantage of the updates right away. Let's all take a breather today and enjoy the win before we dive into the next sprint. Great work, team! Best, Daniel

evidence.title: Re: DevConf sponsorship — decision needed by Friday
evidence.text: # Re: DevConf sponsorship — decision needed by Friday Hey Omar and Claire, Thanks for putting together the breakdown for the upcoming developer meetup series. I've had a chance to look over the proposal from the organizers, and while I think community engagement is important right now, I don't think we need to go all-in on the top-tier package right out of the gate. Let's go with the smaller sponsorship tier instead. It still gives us the logo placement and community table we wanted, but it frees up some budget for our other experiments this quarter without overcommitting before we see what kind of turnout they actually get. Let me know if you need any help adjusting the paperwork or reaching back out to the organizers to lock that tier in. Thanks! Best, Daniel
